title: Seven cards became three life
era: 1994 U.S. Nationals Type I control inspired representative table
matchup: Mind Twist/Rack Control against creature pressure
story: I reached my upkeep with seven cards in hand and Ivory Tower on the battlefield. My opponent had been attacking through my defenses, leaving me at nine life. The Tower trigger counted seven cards, subtracted four, and gave me three life, moving me to twelve. Only after that did I go to my draw step and draw normally. Ancestral Recall remained among the options in my hand, and The Rack was already pressuring the other side. The Tower had not tapped or drawn anything; it merely paid me for holding cards at the right moment.
review: Seven hand cards at Tower trigger resolution, gain 7-4=3 life, 9->12, before normal draw. Does not tap or grant extra draw. Source deck contains Tower, Ancestral Recall, The Rack. 65-card original documented main.
claim: representative reconstruction; not a historical match or quotation
